'''Nicolas Gisin''' (born 29 May 1952) is a Swiss [[physicist]] and [[professor]] at the [[University of Geneva]], working on the foundations of [[quantum mechanics]], [[quantum information|information]], and [[quantum communication|communication]]. His work includes both [[experimental physics|experimental]] and [[theoretical physics]]. He has contributed work in the fields of experimental [[quantum cryptography]] and long-distance [[quantum communication]] over standard telecom [[optical fiber]]s. He also co-founded [[ID Quantique]], a company that provides quantum-based technologies.

==Biography==
Nicolas Gisin was born in [[Geneva]], Switzerland, on 29 May 1952. He received a degree in mathematics and a master's degree in physics before receiving his Ph.D. in Physics from the [[University of Geneva]] in 1981. His dissertation concerned [[Quantum mechanics|quantum]] and [[statistical physics]]. After several years in the software and optical communication industries, Gisin joined the [http://www.unige.ch/sciences/physique/physics-section/research/department-applied-physics/ Group of Applied Physics at the University of Geneva] in 1994, where he started working in optics. Since 2000, he has been the Director of the Department of Applied Physics,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nicolas Gisin |url=https://www.unige.ch/gap/quantum/members:nicolas_gisin |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=www.unige.ch}}</ref> leading a research group in [[Quantum information]] and quantum communication. The [[European Research Council]] awarded him with two successive ERC Advanced Grants.<ref>[http://erc.europa.eu/projects-and-results/erc-funded-projects/qore ERC Quantum Correlations]{{Dead link|date=April 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>[http://erc.europa.eu/projects-and-results/erc-funded-projects/mec ERC Macroscopic Entanglement in Crystals]{{Dead link|date=April 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In 2009, he received the first biennial [[John Stewart Bell Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://cqiqc.physics.utoronto.ca/bell_prize/Gisin.html |title=First John Stewart Bell Prize ceremony |access-date=2015-09-28 |archive-date=2017-06-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622014630/http://cqiqc.physics.utoronto.ca/bell_prize/Gisin.html }}</ref> and, in 2011, he received the prize of the Geneva City.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ville-ge.ch/culture/prixVdG11/r_2007.html |title=Prix de la Ville de Genève |access-date=2015-09-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304110000/http://www.ville-ge.ch/culture/prixVdG11/r_2007.html |archive-date=2016-03-04 }}</ref> In 2014, Switzerland awarded him the Swiss Science prize sponsored by the [[Marcel Benoist Prize|Foundation Marcel Benoist]]<ref>[https://mediaserver.unige.ch/play/86377 Video of the Marcel Benoist Prize Ceremony]</ref> and delivered by the National Government.

On 17 July 2014, Gisin published his book, ''Quantum Chance: Nonlocality, Teleportation, and Other Quantum Marvels'', in which he explains modern quantum physics and its applications without using mathematics or difficult concepts.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Gislim |first=Nicolas |title=Quantum Chance: Nonlocality, Teleportation and Other Quantum Marvels |publisher=Springer International |year=2014}}</ref> The text has been translated from French into English, German, Chinese, Korean, and Russian.

Gisin played [[field hockey]] at the highest Swiss level and was president of [http://www.servettehc.ch/ Servette HC] from 2000 to 2015, furthering his club to become the largest in Switzerland. In 2010 Servette HC was awarded the title "Club of the Year" by the [[European Hockey Federation]].<ref>[http://www.eurohockey.org/welcome/2012-eurohockey-club-year-letter/ EuroHockey Club Of The Year]</ref><ref>[http://www.servettehc.ch/index.php?option=com_ponygallery&Itemid=4&func=viewcategory&catid=182 Photos of the EuroHockey Club Of the Year]</ref> In 2014, the team won the Swiss championship for the first time in its century-long history.

==Research==
* In 1995,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Experimental demonstration of quantum cryptography using polarized photons in optical-fiber over more than 1 km|first1=A.|last1=Muller|first2=J.|last2=Bréguet|first3=N.|last3=Gisin|journal=Europhys. Lett.|volume=23|issue=6|page=383|date=1993|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/23/6/001|doi=10.1209/0295-5075/23/6/001|bibcode=1993EL.....23..383M |s2cid=121806881 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Underwater quantum coding|first1=A.|last1=Muller|first2=H.|last2=Zbinden|first3=N.|last3=Gisin|journal=Nature|volume=378|page=449|date=1995|issue=6556 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/378449a0.pdf|doi=10.1038/378449a0|bibcode=1995Natur.378..449M |s2cid=4237561 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Quantum cryptography over 23 km in installed under-lake telecom fibre|first1=A.|last1=Muller|first2=H.|last2=Zbinden|first3=N.|last3=Gisin|journal=Europhys. Lett.|volume=33|issue=5|page=335|date=1996|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/epl/i1996-00343-4|doi=10.1209/epl/i1996-00343-4|bibcode=1996EL.....33..335M |s2cid=250916473 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Gisin transmitted a [[Quantum cryptography|quantum cryptographic]] signal at a distance of 23 km over a commercial optical fiber under Lake Geneva. Later, his group extended this record to 67 km <ref>{{cite journal|title=Quantum Key Distribution over 67 km with a plug&play system|first1=D.|last1=Stucki|first2=N.|last2=Gisin|first3=O.|last3=Guinnard|first4=G.|last4=Ribordy|first5=H.|last5=Zbinden|journal=New Journal of Physics|volume=4|page=41|date=2002|issue=1 |article-number=341 |doi=10.1088/1367-2630/4/1/341|arxiv=quant-ph/0203118 |bibcode=2002NJPh....4...41S |s2cid=16704961 }}</ref> and 307 km <ref>{{cite journal|title=Provably secure and practical quantum key distribution over 307 km of optical fibre|first1=B.|last1=Korzh|journal= Nature Photonics|volume=9|pages=163–168|date=2015|display-authors=etal|issue=3 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nphoton.2014.327|doi=10.1038/nphoton.2014.327|url-access=subscription|arxiv=1407.7427|bibcode=2015NaPho...9..163K |s2cid=59028718 }}</ref> using Plug-&-Play and Coherent One Way configurations for quantum key distribution.
* In 1997, Nicolas Gisin and his group demonstrated [[Bell inequality|Bell inequality violations]] at a distance of over 10 km.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Violation of Bell inequalities by photons more than 10 km apart|first1=W.|last1=Tittel|first2=J.|last2=Brendel|first3=H.|last3=Zbinden|first4=N.|last4=Gisin|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=81|pages=3563–3566|date=1998|issue=17 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.3563|arxiv=quant-ph/9806043 |bibcode=1998PhRvL..81.3563T |s2cid=55712217 }}</ref> This was the first time when [[Quantum nonlocality|quantum non-locality]] was demonstrated outside the lab; the distance was increased by about three orders of magnitude with respect to all previous experiments. This was followed by further experiments, ever strengthening the conclusion by excluding more and more sophisticated alternative models to quantum theory.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Long-distance Bell-type tests using energy-time entangled photons|first1=W.|last1=Tittel|first2=J.|last2=Brendel|first3=N.|last3=Gisin|first4=H.|last4=Zbinden|journal=Phys. Rev. A|volume=59|pages=4150–4163|date=1999|issue=6 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.59.4150|arxiv=quant-ph/9809025 |bibcode=1999PhRvA..59.4150T |s2cid=119095575 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Bell inequality and the locality loophole: Active versus passive switches|first1=N.|last1=Gisin|first2=H.|last2=Zbinden|journal=Phys. Lett. A|volume=264|pages=103–107|date=1999|issue=2–3 |doi=10.1016/S0375-9601(99)00807-5|arxiv=quant-ph/9906049 |bibcode=1999PhLA..264..103G |s2cid=15383228 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Experimental test of nonlocal quantum correlation in relativistic configurations|first1=H.|last1=Zbinden|first2=J.|last2=Brendel|first3=N.|last3=Gisin|first4=W.|last4=Tittel|journal=Physical Review A|volume=63|issue=2|date=2001|article-number=022111 |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/25289299.pdf|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.63.022111|arxiv=quant-ph/0007009 |bibcode=2001PhRvA..63b2111Z |s2cid=44611890 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Quantum correlations with spacelike separated beam splitters in motion: Experimental test of multisimultaneity|first1=A.|last1=Stefanov|first2=H.|last2=Zbinden|first3=N.|last3=Gisin|first4=A.|last4=Suarez|journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.|volume=88|article-number=120404|date=2002|issue=12 |url=https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=5c635ccb5bda1d51c8238949c4ce1bc413fce7ad|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.88.120404|pmid=11909434 |arxiv=quant-ph/0110117|bibcode=2002PhRvL..88l0404S |s2cid=119522191 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Testing the speed of 'spooky action at a distance'|first1=D.|last1=Salart|first2=A.|last2=Baas|first3=C.|last3=Branciard|first4=N|last4=Gisin|first5=H.|last5=Zbinden|journal=Nature|volume=454|pages=861–864|date=2008|issue=7206 |doi=10.1038/nature07121|pmid=18704081 |arxiv=0808.3316 |bibcode=2008Natur.454..861S |s2cid=4401216 }}</ref>
* In the early 2000s he was the first in demonstrating quantum teleportation over long distances.<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1038/nature01376| issn = 1476-4687| volume = 421| issue = 6922| pages = 509–513| last1 = Marcikic| first1 = I.| last2 = de Riedmatten| first2 = H.| last3 = Tittel| first3 = W.| last4 = Zbinden| first4 = H.| last5 = Gisin| first5 = N.| title = Long-distance teleportation of qubits at telecommunication wavelengths| journal = Nature| access-date = 2023-07-26| date = 2003| pmid = 12556886| url = https://www.nature.com/articles/nature01376| arxiv = quant-ph/0301178| bibcode = 2003Natur.421..509M| s2cid = 118877331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1364/JOSAB.24.000398| issn = 1520-8540| volume = 24| issue = 2| pages = 398–403| last1 = Landry| first1 = Olivier| last2 = Houwelingen| first2 = J. A. W. van| last3 = Beveratos| first3 = Alexios| last4 = Zbinden| first4 = Hugo| last5 = Gisin| first5 = Nicolas| title = Quantum teleportation over the Swisscom telecommunication network| journal = JOSA B| access-date = 2023-07-26| date = 2007-02-01| url = https://opg.optica.org/josab/abstract.cfm?uri=josab-24-2-398| arxiv = quant-ph/0605010| bibcode = 2007JOSAB..24..398L| s2cid = 1377852}}</ref> In the latter experiment the receiving photon was hundreds of meters away when the [[Bell state]] measurement that triggers the teleportation process was performed.
* The previous breakthroughs would not have been possible without single-photon detectors compatible with telecommunication optical fibers. When Gisin entered the field such detectors did not exist. Today, thanks to Gisin and his group at the University of Geneva,<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1364/AO.37.002272| issn = 2155-3165| volume = 37| issue = 12| pages = 2272–2277| last1 = Ribordy| first1 = Grégoire| last2 = Gautier| first2 = Jean-Daniel| last3 = Zbinden| first3 = Hugo| last4 = Gisin| first4 = Nicolas| title = Performance of InGaAs/InP avalanche photodiodes as gated-mode photon counters| journal = Applied Optics| date = 1998-04-20| pmid = 18273153| arxiv = quant-ph/0605042| bibcode = 1998ApOpt..37.2272R}}</ref> single-photon detectors at telecom wavelengths are commercially available.
* Nicolas Gisin's work pushed optical fiber quantum communication almost to its limits. To go further one needs quantum memories and repeaters. His group invented an original [[quantum memory]] protocol using rare earth doped crystals<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1103/PhysRevA.79.052329| volume = 79| issue = 5| article-number = 052329| last1 = Afzelius| first1 = Mikael| last2 = Simon| first2 = Christoph| last3 = de Riedmatten| first3 = Hugues| last4 = Gisin| first4 = Nicolas| title = Multimode quantum memory based on atomic frequency combs| journal = Physical Review A| date = 2009-05-21| arxiv = 0805.4164| bibcode = 2009PhRvA..79e2329A| s2cid = 55205943}}</ref> and used it to demonstrate the first solid state quantum memory.<ref>A solid-state light-matter interface at the single-photon level, H. de Riedmatten, M. Afzelius, M. Staudt, Ch. Simon and N. Gisin, Nature, 456, 773-777 (2008).</ref> Recently they entangled: first a photon with such a crystal,<ref>Quantum storage of photonic [[quantum entanglement|entanglement]] in a crystal, Ch. Clausen, I. Usmani, F. Bussieres, N. Sangouard, M. Afzelius, H. de Riedmatten and N. Gisin, Nature, 469, 508-511 (2011).</ref> next two such crystals<ref name="Heralded">Heralded quantum entanglement between two crystals, I. Usmani, Ch. Clausen, F. Bussieres, N. Sangouard, M. Afzelius and N. Gisin, Nature Photonics 6, 234-237 (2012).</ref> and finally teleported a photonic qubit into a solid-state quantum memory over a distance of 25&nbsp;km.<ref>Quantum teleportation from a telecom-wavelength photon to a solid-state quantum memory, F. Bussières, Ch. Clausen et al., Nature Photonics 8, 775-778 (2014).</ref>
* [[Schrödinger's equation]] is a basic law of nature. Yet one may envisage that at a certain moment in the future novel discoveries may lead to its modification. The most natural such modification is introduction of non-linear terms. Another "Gisin theorem" states however that all deterministic nonlinear modifications of the Schrödinger equation necessarily activate quantum non-locality, leading to true violations of relativity.<ref>Stochastic quantum dynamics and relativity, N. Gisin, Helvetica Physica Acta 62, 363-371 (1989).</ref><ref>Relevant and irrelevant nonlinear Schrodinger equations, N. Gisin and M. Rigo, Phys. A, 28, 7375- 7390 (1995).</ref>
* One of the most important characteristics of quantum information is the [[no-cloning theorem]]. Nicolas Gisin derived a bound on the fidelity of approximate quantum cloning from the relativistic no-signaling constraint.<ref>Quantum cloning without signalling, N. Gisin, Phys. Lett. A 242, 1 (1998).</ref>
* Nicolas Gisin contributed to relating non-locality to the security of quantum key distribution, notably with [[Antonio Acín]], [[Valério Scarani]], [[Nicolas Brunner]] and [[Stephano Pironio]].<ref>From Bell's theorem to secure quantum key distribution, A. Acin, N. Gisin and L. Masanes, Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 120405 (2006).</ref><ref>Device-independent security of quantum cryptography against collective attacks, A. Acin, N. Brunner, N. Gisin, S. Massar, S. Pironio and V. Scarani, Phys. Rev. Lett. 98, 230501 (2007).</ref><ref>Device-independent quantum key distribution secure against collective attacks, S. Pironio, A. Acin, N. Brunner, N. Gisin, S. Massar and V. Scarani, New Journal of Physics, 11, 1-25 (2009).</ref> This opened an entirely new field of research known as Device Independent Quantum Information Processing (DI-QIP).
* In 1984, Nicolas Gisin's proposed stochastic Schrödinger equations<ref>Quantum measurements and stochastic processes, N. Gisin, Phys. Rev. Lett. 52, 1657 (1984).</ref> and his subsequent work with [[Ian C. Percival]] is now widely used in the study of the dynamics of open quantum systems.<ref>The Quantum State Diffusion model applied to open systems, N. Gisin and I.C. Percival, J. Phys. A, 25, 5677-5691 (1992).</ref>
* Gisin invented a technique to measure Polarization Mode Dispersion (PMD) in optical fibers.<ref>Polarization mode dispersion of short and long single mode fibers, N. Gisin, J.P. Von Der Weid and J.P. Pellaux, IEEE J. Lightwave Technology, 9, 821-827 (1991).</ref><ref>Polarization mode dispersion: Time domain versus Frequency domain, N. Gisin and J.P. Pellaux, Optics Commun., 89, 316-323 (1992).</ref> This turned out to be an extremely important parameter of telecom fibers whose importance was initially underestimated. The technique was adopted as an international standard and was transferred to industry (first to a spin-off, next to the Canadian company EXFO). Still today it is the most used technique to characterize PMD. Being both a classical and quantum engineer, he applied the abstract concepts of quantum weak values to the field of classical telecommunication networks.<ref>Optical Telecom Networks as Weak Quantum Measurements with Post-selection, N. Brunner, A. Acin, D.Collins, N. Gisin et V. Scarani, Physical Review Letters,  91, 180402 (2003).</ref>
* In 2019, Nicolas Gisin demonstrated the existence of a new form of nonlocality in quantum networks<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Renou |first1=Marc-Olivier |last2=Bäumer |first2=Elisa |last3=Boreiri |first3=Sadra |last4=Brunner |first4=Nicolas |last5=Gisin |first5=Nicolas |last6=Beigi |first6=Salman |title=Genuine Quantum Nonlocality in the Triangle Network |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=123 |issue=14 |article-number=140401 |date=September 2019 |issn=1079-7114 |doi=10.1103/physrevlett.123.140401 |publisher=American Physical Society (APS) |pmid=31702202 |arxiv=1905.04902 |bibcode=2019PhRvL.123n0401R }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Pusey |first=Matthew F. |title=Quantum Correlations Take a New Shape |journal=Physics |volume=12 |issue=106 |date=September 30, 2019 |article-number=106 |url=https://physics.aps.org/articles/v12/106 |publisher=American Physical Society |location=York, United Kingdom |doi=10.1103/Physics.12.106 |bibcode=2019PhyOJ..12..106P }}</ref>
* In 2021, Nicolas Gisin proved that Real Quantum Theory, the theory obtained from quantum theory when complex numbers are replaced with real ones, cannot explain all the correlations which can be obtained in quantum networks,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Renou |first1=Marc-Olivier |last2=Trillo |first2=David |last3=Weilenmann |first3=Mirjam |last4=Le |first4=Thinh P. |last5=Tavakoli |first5=Armin |last6=Gisin |first6=Nicolas |last7=Acín |first7=Antonio |last8=Navascués |first8=Miguel |title=Quantum theory based on real numbers can be experimentally falsified |journal=Nature |volume=600 |issue=7890 |pages=625–629 |date=December 2021 |issn=1476-4687 |doi=10.1038/s41586-021-04160-4 |publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC |pmid=34912122 |pmc=8695381 |arxiv=2101.10873 |bibcode=2021Natur.600..625R }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Renou |first1=Marc-Olivier |last2=Acín |first2=Antonio |last3=Navascués |first3=Miguel |title=Quantum Physics Falls Apart without Imaginary Numbers |journal=Scientific American|date=1 April 2023 |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/quantum-physics-falls-apart-without-imaginary-numbers/ |language=en }}</ref> notably with [[Antonio Acín]].
